raw: {"analysis":"DGS provides a more complete and operationally sound plan. It correctly sequences the work with clear gates, mandates pre-migration backups, handles the CI flake pragmatically, and explicitly avoids touching the shared validation library. QZS has a critical timing flaw: it suggests merging to main only after the previous day's export completes, which would push the fix past the next nightly export window and leave marketing blocked longer than necessary. QZS also introduces ambiguity around whether a staging clone or snapshot is used, and its human decision point on checksum mismatch is dangerously permissive when data integrity is the core requirement.","verdict":"DGS"}
